02F-02 · Leaks

Fix

One leak is one leak. The report says so.

Leaks traced and opened up, with photos of what we found and how it was closed. If the rest of the slope is sound, the call is watch, and the price is a repair, not a roof.

When it's more than one leak: curled, cracked shingles across a whole slope get their own finding, and the report tells you how many years that slope has left.

Low-slope coating. Flat porch or patio holding water? Silicone coating on flat porch and patio sections to stop ponding leaks and bounce summer sun.

04F-04 · Hail claim help

How a hail claim goes in Texas, step by step.

No promises about what your insurer pays. Just the order things happen in, so nobody rushes you into signing.

Hail hits measured, chalked and photographed so your adjuster sees the same roof we saw.

  1. 1

    Storm

    Hail or wind rolls through. Write down the date and photograph anything on the ground.

  2. 2

    Inspection

    We get on the roof, chalk the hits and photograph each one. You get the report first.

  3. 3

    Claim filed

    You call your insurer with the storm date. The report backs up what you tell them.

  4. 4

    Adjuster visit

    We can meet the adjuster on the roof and walk the same diagram, finding by finding.

  5. 5

    First check

    Usually the claim minus depreciation and minus your deductible. The deductible is yours to pay.

  6. 6

    Build

    Tear-off, decking photos, new roof. Anything new we find gets its own photo and line.

  7. 7

    Final invoice

    The invoice goes to your insurer with the build photos attached.

  8. 8

    Depreciation released

    The money held back is paid once the work is shown done.

Book the inspection before you call your insurer Or ask us on the phone first

Read this before anyone knocks

We won't touch your deductible. Texas law says we can't, and we'd rather tell you now.

Anyone offering to waive it or "cover it" is asking you to sign a claim that isn't true. Texas Insurance Code, chapter 707.
